workbench_tag_assign: Stores a value in a variable. Filters can transform the value before assignment.
workbench_tag_capture: Renders the body and stores its text in a variable. Close the block with endcapture.
workbench_tag_endcapture: Closes a capture block. The rendered text becomes the capture variable's value.
workbench_tag_for: Renders the body once per item in a collection. Use forloop for the current index, first, and last flags. An else branch handles an empty collection.
workbench_tag_endfor: Closes a for loop. Rendering continues with the next item, or after the loop when all items are processed.
workbench_tag_if: Renders the body when the condition is true. Only false and nil are falsy in Liquid; compare with blank or empty to check missing content.
workbench_tag_endif: Closes an if block, including any elsif and else branches.
workbench_tag_unless: Renders the body when the condition is false. Close the block with endunless.
workbench_tag_endunless: Closes an unless block, including any elsif and else branches.
workbench_tag_else: Provides the fallback branch in if, unless, or case, or the empty-collection branch in for.
workbench_tag_elsif: Tests another condition when the preceding if or unless branch was skipped.
workbench_tag_case: Compares a value with each when branch and renders matching branches. An else branch handles values with no match.
workbench_tag_when: Starts a matching branch in a case block. Separate alternative values with or or commas.
workbench_tag_endcase: Closes a case block and its when and else branches.
workbench_tag_break: Stops the current for loop immediately. Rendering continues after endfor.
workbench_tag_continue: Skips the rest of the current for iteration and starts the next item.
workbench_tag_cycle: Outputs the next value in a repeating list. An optional group name keeps separate cycles independent.
workbench_tag_increment: Outputs a counter, then increases it by one. The first output is 0. Counters are separate from variables made with assign or capture.
workbench_tag_decrement: Decreases a counter by one, then outputs it. The first output is -1. Counters are separate from variables made with assign or capture.
workbench_tag_echo: Outputs a value, with optional filters. Useful for output inside a multiline liquid block.
workbench_tag_render: Renders a registered partial in an isolated scope. Pass data explicitly with named arguments or with … as …; for … as … repeats the partial for a collection.
workbench_tag_include: Renders a registered partial with access to the caller's variables. Use render when the partial needs an isolated scope.
workbench_tag_layout: Renders this template inside a registered layout. Named block tags supply content for the layout's matching blocks.
workbench_tag_block: Defines a layout block or replaces its content in a template that uses the layout. The block name is optional; close with endblock.
workbench_tag_endblock: Closes a layout block and finishes its content.
workbench_tag_tablerow: Renders a collection as HTML table rows and cells. Set cols to control the number of columns and place the block inside a table element.
workbench_tag_endtablerow: Closes a tablerow loop and finishes its generated table cells and rows.
workbench_tag_raw: Outputs the body literally, including Liquid delimiters. Liquid expressions inside the block stay unevaluated.
workbench_tag_endraw: Closes a raw block. Liquid processing resumes after this tag.
workbench_tag_comment: Omits the body from the output and skips the Liquid code inside it. Close the block with endcomment.
workbench_tag_endcomment: Closes a comment block. Rendering resumes after this tag.
workbench_tag_inline_comment: Omits comment text from the output. Each comment line starts with #, including inside a multiline liquid block.
workbench_tag_liquid: Groups Liquid tags in one block. Write one tag per line, without individual delimiters. Use echo to output a value.
workbench_tag_bq: Renders the body as a Markdown blockquote. ZotLit trims the outer whitespace, prefixes lines with >, and reduces consecutive blank lines to one. Close with endbq.
workbench_tag_endbq: Closes ZotLit's bq block. The rendered body becomes a Markdown blockquote.
workbench_tag_suffix: Adds a random suffix only when the note name already exists at creation. Use in the filename expression. Defaults: 6 characters, '_' before, and no text after. Length must be 1–64; affixes cannot contain : or %.
workbench_tag_render_annotation: Renders the Profile's final annotation section with the argument bound to zt in an isolated scope. Outside a Profile, uses the named annotation partial. The argument must be present and non-null.
workbench_tag_managed: Marks the note content ZotLit replaces on update. A Profile can have one managed block in its note body. It renders in an isolated scope. Keep both boundaries as explicit tags, outside multiline liquid blocks.
workbench_tag_endmanaged: Closes the managed block. Note content after this boundary is kept during updates. Use this explicit tag outside multiline liquid blocks.

workbench_problem_unsupported_js: The property '{key}' runs JavaScript, which the web workbench can't evaluate.
workbench_problem_unsupported_js_unnamed: One property runs JavaScript, which the web workbench can't evaluate.

workbench_problem_invalid_document: This file is not a profile document.
workbench_problem_invalid_document_recov: A profile opens with a YAML manifest between two “---” lines.
workbench_problem_invalid_manifest_field: The manifest field '{field}' is not valid.
workbench_problem_invalid_manifest_recov: Correct the highlighted YAML in the manifest.
workbench_problem_invalid_managed_block: The managed block is not opened and closed correctly.
workbench_problem_invalid_managed_block_: Keep one open tag and one close tag around the managed block.
workbench_problem_duplicate_managed_bloc: Your note has more than one managed block.
Keep at most one managed block in your note.
workbench_problem_unknown_section_header: This line is not a profile section header.
Use only the standalone “--- zotlit:annotation ---” header. Your note starts after the manifest.
workbench_problem_duplicate_annotation_s: This profile has more than one annotation section.
Keep one “--- zotlit:annotation ---” header, followed by the annotation source.
workbench_problem_missing_annotation_sec: This profile has no annotation section.
Add one standalone “--- zotlit:annotation ---” line after your note. The annotation source can be empty.
workbench_problem_reserved_annotation_pa: The partial name 'annotation' is reserved for the annotation section.
Rename that partial and update the calls to it.
